<!-- Generated by tools/oracle/render_license_docs.py from tools/oracle/manifest.json. Do not edit by hand. -->

Each folder holds verbatim licence, notice and policy files fetched at the pinned upstream revision
recorded in `tools/oracle/manifest.json` (re-fetch with `tools/oracle/fetch_vocab.py`).
The one exception is a `.txt` file whose manifest source type is `html-text`: it is a deterministic
plain-text extraction of the HTML page snapshotted next to it (e.g. the Gemma Terms of Use).
Obligations are plain-language summaries for planning, not legal advice; the snapshot text governs.

Ship intent:

- `ship`: a file derived from this asset is planned for the public site.
- `oracle-only`: used locally or in CI as a reference implementation only; never redistributed.
- `phase-2`: a candidate for a later phase; needs owner sign-off before shipping.

## openai-o200k_base

o200k_base BPE rank file (tiktoken format) used by GPT-4o/4.1/5.x; GPT-6 assumed but unconfirmed.

- **Lab:** OpenAI
- **SPDX:** `MIT`
- **Ship intent:** `ship` (primary OpenAI tokenizer)
- **Licence source (pinned):** <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/openai/tiktoken/a1a9f16826f3f2d8ba80b6c5fd270c1c340d6d67/LICENSE>
- **Snapshots:** [LICENSE](openai-o200k_base/LICENSE) (license)
- **Obligations:**
  - Include the tiktoken MIT licence ("Copyright (c) 2022 OpenAI, Shantanu Jain" plus the permission notice, docs/licenses/openai-o200k_base/LICENSE) with the shipped rank data, e.g. on the site's licences page.
  - Disclose that the .tiktoken rank file carries no licence statement of its own and is redistributed on the basis of the MIT-licensed tiktoken project that defines and downloads it (owner to confirm).

Provenance notes: Azure blob host has no revision system: pinned by ETag and Last-Modified (2024-05-13); its Content-MD5 header is recorded and verified on every download. 199,998 rank lines; sha256 and size match research section 3.1; tiktoken 0.14.0 encode_ordinary('台灣台南') = [3735, 133072, 3735, 14609] (research section 5.3) reproduced. The host sends no CORS headers, so the site must self-host. The rank file itself carries no explicit licence statement; the LICENSE snapshot is tiktoken's (openai/tiktoken, last changed in a1a9f168, 2022-12-14).

Provenance notes: Ungated HF repo pinned at ee0ef602 (lastModified 2026-07-20). tokenizer.json sha256 cc8d3a0c… and size equal research; the HF X-Linked-ETag shows the same file in gemma-4-E2B-it, -12B-it, -26B-A4B-it and -31B-it. 262,144 vocab, 514,906 merges, 24 added tokens, byte_fallback=true. NO LICENSE FILE: none of the five Gemma 4 -it repos contains a LICENSE or NOTICE. Licence evidence: the model card front matter (README.md snapshot) says license: apache-2.0 with license_link https://ai.google.dev/gemma/docs/gemma_4_license; that page (301 to /gemma/apache_2, Last-Modified 2026-04-01, banner 'This documentation is deprecated. Please visit the new documentation at gemma.ai') contains Apache License 2.0 sections 1-9 verbatim, identical to apache.org up to 'END OF TERMS AND CONDITIONS'. Verdict: plain Apache-2.0. The licence snapshot is therefore apache.org's LICENSE-2.0.txt (no revision system; pinned by ETag).

## google-gemma2

Gemma 1/2 SentencePiece model (tokenizer/tokenizer.model, 256,000 pieces) from google/gemma_pytorch; the Vertex AI SDK's local tokenizer maps Gemini 1.0/1.5 to this exact file.

- **Lab:** Google DeepMind
- **SPDX:** `Apache-2.0 (repo) + LicenseRef-Gemma-Terms-of-Use (applicability unresolved)`
- **Ship intent:** `ship` (secondary Google tokenizer for Gemini 1.0/1.5 (owner decision); ship with the Gemma Terms pass-through package (Terms copy, Notice file, §3.2 restrictions, modification notice) until applicability is resolved)
- **Licence source (pinned):** <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/google/gemma_pytorch/33b652c465537c6158f9a472ea5700e5e770ad3f/LICENSE>
- **Snapshots:** [LICENSE](google-gemma2/LICENSE) (license), [gemma-terms-of-use.html](google-gemma2/gemma-terms-of-use.html) (license-evidence), [gemma-terms-of-use.txt](google-gemma2/gemma-terms-of-use.txt) (license)
- **Obligations:**
  - Include a copy of the Apache License 2.0 (docs/licenses/google-gemma2/LICENSE, the google/gemma_pytorch repo licence at 33b652c4) with the shipped tokenizer or any asset derived from it, and state changes (e.g. conversion to a compact format).
  - Gemma Terms pass-through, use restrictions (§3.1(1) and §3.2): include the Section 3.2 use restrictions (the Gemma Prohibited Use Policy at ai.google.dev/gemma/prohibited_use_policy, incorporated by reference, and no use in violation of applicable law) as an enforceable provision in the terms governing the shipped tokenizer, and tell recipients that it is subject to them.
  - Gemma Terms pass-through, copy of the Agreement (§3.1(2)): give every recipient a copy of the Gemma Terms of Use (docs/licenses/google-gemma2/gemma-terms-of-use.txt), e.g. on the site's licences page.
  - Gemma Terms pass-through, modification notice (§3.1(3)): every modified file (e.g. a compact re-serialisation of tokenizer.model) must carry a prominent notice stating that it was modified.
  - Gemma Terms pass-through, Notice file (§3.1(4)): accompany every Distribution other than a Hosted Service with a "Notice" text file containing: "Gemma is provided under and subject to the Gemma Terms of Use found at ai.google.dev/gemma/terms".
  - Gemma Terms, Google's remote-restriction right (§3.2): Google reserves the right to restrict (remotely or otherwise) usage it reasonably believes violates the Agreement, and may terminate it on breach (§4.5); be ready to withdraw the asset.
  - Applicability unresolved: the Terms define Gemma as models, weights and parameters and never mention tokenizers, while the same file sits in the Apache-2.0 repo. The pass-through items above are the conservative default until the owner or legal decides.

Provenance notes: GitHub google/gemma_pytorch pinned at 33b652c4 (2024-02-21, 'Removing typos and launch day cleanup'), the latest commit touching tokenizer/tokenizer.model. It is also the exact URL and sha256 (61a7b147…) that the Vertex AI SDK local tokenizer (googleapis/python-aiplatform vertexai/tokenization/_tokenizer_loading.py, main branch read 2026-10-25) pins for gemini-1.0-pro and gemini-1.5-pro/flash. tokenizer.model is a plain git blob (not LFS): 4,241,003 B, matching research section 3.3; 256,000 pieces (sentencepiece 0.2.2): NORMAL 255,495, USER_DEFINED 245, BYTE 256 at ids 217-472 (derived from the piece types; matches research sections 3.3 and 5.2), CONTROL 3 (&lt;pad&gt; 0, &lt;eos&gt; 1, &lt;bos&gt; 2), UNK 1 (&lt;unk&gt; 3); identity normaliser, add_dummy_prefix=false, split_digits=true. The research found the official Gemma 1 and Gemma 2 tokenizer.model files byte-identical. Byte id 226 is &lt;0x09&gt; in the .model, but the HF tokenizer.json for Gemma 1/2 keys it as a literal tab (research section 5.2). Research anchors reproduced: 台灣台南 -&gt; [40911, 139274], 東京都渋谷区 -&gt; [98973, 101041, 236149]. LICENSE fetched at the same commit: Apache-2.0, byte-identical to the google-gemma3-spiece snapshot (sha256 c71d239d…, 11,357 B). Gemma Terms of Use retrieved 2026-10-25 from https://ai.google.dev/gemma/terms (Last-Modified Wed, 01 Apr 2026 21:33:57 GMT; the page says 'Last modified: April 1, 2026'); its Appendix lists Gemma 1, 1.1 and 2, and it points Gemma 4 to the Apache-2.0 Gemma 4 licence. The host sends no ETag and every response embeds a fresh CSP nonce and feature-flag order, so the raw HTML snapshot (gemma-terms-of-use.html, marked volatile) can never be re-downloaded byte-identically; gemma-terms-of-use.txt is the deterministic plain-text extraction (page title plus article body, oracle_lib/htmltext.py) and is identical across requests. Section 3.2 incorporates the Gemma Prohibited Use Policy (ai.google.dev/gemma/prohibited_use_policy), which is not snapshotted here.

The tarball is pinned by the registry dist.integrity (sha512, verified on every fetch); registry shasum d1f5dab07bbf9289414dad1f7c57b812b27bb857. LICENCE CONFLICT CONFIRMED: package.json 'license' is 'Apache-2.0', but the LICENSE file is the MIT permission notice ('Copyright 2023 Anthropic, PBC.', with no 'MIT License' title line); spdx records the LICENSE file. claude.json (size matches research): bpe_ranks in tiktoken '!'-compressed form, 64,995 ranks at ids 5-64999 plus 5 specials (&lt;EOT&gt;=0 … &lt;SOS&gt;=4), all 256 single bytes present, pat_str without (?i:). Caveat: the file's own explicit_n_vocab field is 64,739, which is inconsistent with its 65,000 ids, so consumers must not rely on it. package/dist/cjs/claude.json in the tarball is byte-identical. This is the Claude 1/2-era vocabulary, not the Claude 3+ tokenizer.
